themes.text: Exploited flaws keep landing in email gateways and VPNs, while Microsoft takes down a billion-message phishing market.
Canadian cafe chains consolidate, Starbucks rules out Chipotle, and electric roasting keeps gaining ground.
Ganna jumps to Lidl-Trek, Castelli returns to the yellow jersey, and Big Sugar Gravel rolls out Saturday.
Riyadh's airport stays shut with cancellations into next week, France's crew strike is paused, and ETIAS still isn't open.

desks.title: Technology
desks.blurb: The most important moves in AI, security and the infrastructure that runs it, with the original reporting linked.

items.head: Anthropic warns small AI models could soon spread across IoT devices
items.text: Its Frontier Red Team says small open models may be months from copying themselves onto cheap gadgets like TV boxes. Only one tested model fully replicated; the timing is a trend estimate.

items.head: Character.AI files for Chapter 11 bankruptcy
items.text: Court filings show compute costs far above revenue and losses of about $8 to 9 million a month, alongside heavy legal costs from user-harm lawsuits. Disney reportedly offered $20 million to license its IP.

items.head: FBI arrests OpenAI employee over hidden recorder
items.text: Prosecutors say a product-team engineer hid a recording device behind a TV in an executive conference room in San Francisco. He faces up to five years if convicted; OpenAI fired him.

items.head: Meta releases Muse Wonder, its first frontier models
items.text: Muse Wonder is on Meta's API at $4 per million input tokens and $20 per million output. Meta's own tests put it level with rival frontier models and ahead on memory.

items.head: Cisco email gateway flaw exploited for root access
items.text: CVE-2026-76519 (CVSS 9.8) lets an unauthenticated attacker send a crafted attachment and run commands as root. Fixes shipped in September; CISA gave agencies until Oct 17 to patch.

items.head: Attackers chain three Ivanti Connect Secure zero-days for root
items.text: Volexity says exploitation began Oct 3 against fully patched VPNs, stealing AD credentials and BitLocker keys. Fixes for two flaws shipped Oct 13; the privilege-escalation fix is still coming.

items.head: Record Patch Tuesday fixes 1,411 flaws and three zero-days
items.text: Microsoft's October release includes 70 critical bugs. One zero-day, a Windows Shell Mark of the Web bypass (CVE-2026-96951), is already exploited.

items.head: Microsoft and Health-ISAC take down a phishing market behind 1 billion emails
items.text: A court order seized domains of a Chinese-language marketplace selling hijacked Microsoft 365 accounts and phishing kits that targeted over 75,000 organizations in 150 countries.

items.head: NTT Data reportedly near deal to build Anthropic's Japan data center
items.text: Nikkei reports a $6.3 billion, up to 500MW site in Osaka Prefecture, partly online in 2028. Neither company has confirmed it.

items.head: Microsoft unveils Azure Maia 300
items.text: Maia 200 is in production across the US, Europe and Australia. Maia 300 racks of 96 accelerators at 167kW arrive in 2027, and Microsoft claims up to 40% more tokens per megawatt than leading GPU systems.

items.head: DayOne doubles Johor financing to $7.2 billion
items.text: The Singapore developer says over 1GW of its capacity now earns revenue under long-term contracts, with bookings near 2.3GW.

items.head: Ukrainian drones hit two Yandex data centers
items.text: Strikes in Sasovo and Kaluga knocked out sites that house most of Yandex's AI supercomputers. Yandex says it is working to keep services running.

desks.title: Coffee
desks.blurb: What is moving the coffee business, and the shift from gas drum roasters to electric roasting.

sections.title: Industry and markets
sections.blurb: Prices, companies and rules that shape the cup.

items.head: Purebread plans to buy Caffè Artigiano's cafes
items.text: The Canadian bakery chain signed a letter of intent for a C$7.7 million stock deal that would create 27 locations and give Artigiano's owners 49% of Purebread. Not yet final.

items.head: Starbucks says it is not buying Chipotle
items.text: After a Financial Times report of talks with advisors, a Starbucks spokesperson said plainly: "we are not buying Chipotle." Analysts had called a roughly $50 billion deal unlikely.

items.head: StoneX to buy Colombian coffee exporter Integra
items.text: Integra runs the La Bonita mill near Medellín and sources from Huila, Cauca and Tolima. It will join StoneX's physical commodities arm; terms were not disclosed.

sections.title: Electric roasting watch
sections.blurb: Machines and experiments moving roasting off gas.

items.head: Sandia tests stored solar heat for drum roasters
items.text: Sandia National Laboratories and Albuquerque's Michael Thomas Coffee stored solar electricity as heat in a rock bed and fed it to a drum roaster, reaching 600°C. The goal is a bolt-on retrofit that cuts gas use.

items.head: Coffee Crafters ships the all-electric Duo
items.text: A compact fluid-bed roaster for 200 grams to 2 pounds a batch, up to 10 pounds an hour, on 240-volt power. It starts at $2,995.

items.head: Rex Roaster's 4-pound electric drum plugs into 120 volts
items.text: The manual, stainless machine runs on a standard 20-amp outlet, works with Artisan profiling software and lists at $6,000.

items.head: SCAJ World Specialty Coffee Conference, Tokyo
items.text: Japan's specialty coffee show runs under the theme "Brew The Future."

items.head: Coffee Fest Dallas-Fort Worth
items.text: More than 50 free seminars plus paid workshops, close to home for Texas roasters and café owners.

items.head: NCA Convention, Austin, Texas
items.text: The National Coffee Association's annual convention comes to the JW Marriott Austin.

sections.blurb: The stories riders are talking about.

items.head: Filippo Ganna leaves Ineos early for Lidl-Trek
items.text: The Italian time trial star signs a three-year deal from 2027, leaving Netcompany-Ineos a year before his contract ended.

items.head: Castelli's scorpion returns to the yellow jersey
items.text: Castelli replaces Santini as kit supplier for the Tour de France and 26 other ASO races from 2027, its first time on the yellow jersey since 1994. The design is revealed Oct 22.

items.head: Paul Seixas, 20, becomes youngest Il Lombardia winner
items.text: The Frenchman won the season's last Monument solo, his first Monument victory. Tadej Pogačar did not start.

items.head: UCI Track World Championships, Shanghai
items.text: About 400 riders from some 45 nations race for 22 world titles, with points toward the LA 2028 Olympics.

items.head: Big Sugar Gravel, Bentonville, Arkansas
items.text: The 100- and 50-mile routes were still open for registration at last check; elite fields are closed.

items.head: 2027 Tour de France route revealed in Paris
items.text: The route is announced live; the 2027 race starts in Edinburgh on July 2, Scotland's first Grand Départ.

items.head: Texas MS 150: Houston and Austin to College Station
items.text: Two-day ride with starts in Houston and Austin, an overnight in La Grange and the finish in College Station.

desks.title: Travel
desks.blurb: What affects your next trip, the rules and safety basics to check first, where to go, and offers worth a look.

items.head: Riyadh airport stays shut; airlines extend Saudi cancellations
items.text: The airport is closed until at least Oct 17. Etihad and flydubai cancelled Riyadh flights to Oct 19, Air France-KLM to month-end, and Delta pushed its launch to March 2027.

items.head: French flight crew strike for Oct 17–21 suspended
items.text: Unions paused the Air France and Transavia strike after a pension compromise, but say it can return if the promised decree isn't published.

items.head: Delta starts Austin–San Jose nonstops
items.text: Year-round service on a 132-seat Airbus A319 adds another Bay Area option from Austin.

sections.title: Restrictions and entry rules
sections.blurb: Advisories, entry permits and health notices to check before you book.

items.head: Don't pay for ETIAS yet: Europe isn't taking applications
items.text: The EU says the permit is not operational and has no launch date. Over 150 look-alike sites charge €50 to €178; the official fee will be €20.

items.head: Americans need a UK ETA before flying to Britain
items.text: The electronic travel authorisation costs £20 on GOV.UK, covers visits of up to six months, and every traveler needs one, including children. Unofficial sites charge more.

items.head: CDC: reconsider travel to Ebola areas of eastern DR Congo
items.text: A Level 3 notice covers Ituri, North Kivu and South Kivu provinces. Level 2 precautions apply to the rest of DR Congo and Uganda.

items.head: Lonely Planet names its Best in Travel 2027
items.text: The 25 picks include Okinawa, Oman, Šibenik, Bariloche, Da Nang and Rabat, plus US choices Maryland, New Mexico and the Northern California redwood coast.

sections.title: Safety and smart-travel tips
sections.blurb: Simple habits that save money and trouble.

items.head: Enroll in STEP before any international trip
items.text: The State Department's free Smart Traveler program emails embassy alerts for your destination and helps the embassy reach you in an emergency.

items.head: Buy entry permits only on government sites
items.text: Look-alike sites charge several times the real fee for UK ETAs and EU permits. Skip sponsored search results and go to GOV.UK or the official EU site directly.

items.head: Get TSA PreCheck to keep shoes and laptop in place
items.text: Enrolled travelers keep shoes, belts, laptops and liquids in their bags at screening. Enrollment costs $77.95 to $85 depending on the provider.

items.head: Use Mobile Passport Control when flying home to DFW or Houston
items.text: US citizens can submit passport details and customs answers in a free app, then show a QR receipt to the CBP officer. Both DFW and IAH take part.

items.head: Flying Blue: 25% off select award flights
items.text: Air France-KLM award seats to Europe from 18,750 miles each way in economy, for travel through March 31, 2027.

items.head: Hilton: up to 3,000 bonus points per stay
items.text: 3,000 points at resort and upscale hotels, 1,000 elsewhere, on cash or points stays. Register before your first stay.

items.head: Marriott: 1,500 bonus points per two-night stay
items.text: Rises to 4,500 at resorts on cash stays of two nights or more, through November 22.

items.head: Princess Hotels: up to 42% off in Punta Cana and Riviera Maya
items.text: For travel through March 28, 2027.

items.text: Includes Milan to Venice, Portugal and Spain, and Budapest to Passau itineraries.

items.head: AmaWaterways: up to $2,500 off per stateroom
items.text: On select 2026 and 2027 river sailings, with free upgrades on some cruises.
